speaker: Kimi K3
text: ICICI Bank's 16% revenue growth and consistent EPS beats make it a quality compounder at 12.6% 5-year CAGR, but that pace needs 19 years to 10x your Rs 10k — well short of your timeline. On the IPO question: US IPOs typically require $2,500+ minimums and allocation is near-zero for $100 accounts, so that route is effectively closed. For Reliance on Zerodha delivery: round-trip costs are 0.38% (STT, stamp duty, exchange fees, DP charge ≈ Rs 38 on Rs 10k), plus 20% short-term capital gains tax if sold within 12 months. Auto and battery plays like Tata Motors, M&M, or Exide trade well under Rs 10k per share, so they're accessible for whole-share purchases.

speaker: Nemotron Ultra
text: ICICI Bank's 16% revenue growth looks solid, but that 81% max drawdown is a reminder that quality compounds can still get cut in half during credit cycles — your Rs 10k would need 19 years at this pace to 10x, and a single bad year resets the clock. On the IPO front, US minimums start around $2,500 so $100 gets you zero allocation; Indian IPOs need 50-share lots, so even a Rs 100 issue price means Rs 5,000 minimum — your Rs 10k could technically apply for one lot, but oversubscription makes allotment a lottery. For Reliance on Zerodha delivery, the round-trip is 0.38% (Rs 38 on Rs 10k) plus 20% STCG tax if held under 12 months; intraday drops the cost to 0.11% but profits become speculative income taxed at your slab. Auto and battery names you can buy whole shares of: Tata Motors (~Rs 750), M&M (~Rs 2,800), Exide (~Rs 350), Amara Raja (~Rs 1,100) — all under your Rs 10k budget per share.
